dampac_chequetan: According to Dampier, the name of a harbour reached before Estapa.
dampac_thelupan: According to Dampier, the name of a settlement near the hill in Chapter IX.
dampac_oarrha: According to Dampier, the name of the place named in the Sallagua coastal account.
dampac_coronada: According to Dampier, the name of the place called Crown-Land.
dampac_purification: According to Dampier, the name of the city near the bay of Valderas.
dampac_cullacan: According to Dampier, the name of a river and district trading with California.
dampac_california: According to Dampier, the name of the region whose insularity Dampier discusses.
dampac_cavalli: According to Dampier, the name of a hill called Horse’s Head by Spanish speakers.
dampac_oleta: According to Dampier, the name of a river on the Pacific coast.
dampac_maxentelba: According to Dampier, the name of a rock in Dampier’s coastal survey.
dampac_zelisco: According to Dampier, the name of a hill in the coastal survey.
dampac_compostella: According to Dampier, the name of a town inland from the river of St. Jago.
dampac_diego: According to Dampier, the name of the owner of the cattle farm east of Port Angels.
dampac_veracruz: According to Dampier, the name of a harbour on the northern coast of New Spain.
dampac_ulloa: According to Dampier, the name of the place named in the harbour of Saint John d’Ulloa.
dampac_lucas: According to Dampier, the name of a cape at the southern end of California.
dampac_narborough: According to Dampier, the name of the English mariner Sir John Narborough.
dampac_guinea: According to Dampier, the name of the region of West Africa named in the comparison of palms.
dampac_caraccos: According to Dampier, the name of the region of the Caribbean coast named in the account of the jewfish.
dampac_maguella: According to Dampier, the name of a valley along the coast searched before Colima.
dampac_lizard: According to Dampier, the name of a cape in England used as the reference meridian.
dampac_valiris: According to Dampier, the name of a valley called Valderas, in the author's proposed alternative reading.
dampac_cavendish: According to Dampier, the name of the English navigator who captured the Manila ship off Cape St. Lucas.
dampac_pastla: According to Dampier, the name of a river that some maps place in Cullacan.
dampac_riosal: According to Dampier, the name of a lake whose Spanish name means river of salt.
dampac_potosi: According to Dampier, the name of a mining town used for the comparison of Mexican silver.
dampac_davisb: According to Dampier, the name of a bay named by Dampier as a starting point for the northern passage.
dampac_hudson: According to Dampier, the name of a bay named for the Canadian approach to the passage.
dampac_korea: According to Dampier, the name of the region near China and Japan.
dampac_tartary: According to Dampier, the name of the region of the northern Asian coast.
dampac_archangel: According to Dampier, the name of a harbour in northern Russia.
dampac_wood: According to Dampier, the name of the captain cited for the ice obstructing a north-east passage.
dampac_drake: According to Dampier, the name of the English navigator compared with Cavendish.
dampac_teat: According to Dampier, the name of the captain commanding the bark under Swan.
dampac_hopenose: According to Dampier, the name of a cape at the southern end of Africa.
dampac_newholland: According to Dampier, the name of the region of the Australian coast called New-Holland in the account.
dampac_indraught: According to Dampier, the name of the region whose Dutch name Dampier interprets as a land that draws ships towards it.
dampac_lopez: According to Dampier, the name of a cape on the coast of Guinea.
dampac_barbadoes: According to Dampier, the name of an island of the West Indies.
dampac_canby: According to Dampier, the name of the ship's mate who describes the voyage between Lopez and Barbadoes.
dampac_norwood: According to Dampier, the name of the surveyor whose land measurements Dampier questions.
dampac_guahon: According to Dampier, the name of an island named Guam, here given its local pronunciation.
dampac_goa: According to Dampier, the name of a town in western India associated here with coconut arrack.
dampac_maldives: According to Dampier, the name of an island group at which coir is prepared for trade.
dampac_timor: According to Dampier, the name of an island supplying the black sort of coir.
dampac_knox: According to Dampier, the name of the captain who wrote the account of Ceylon.
dampac_philip: According to Dampier, the name of the king of Spain from whom the Philippine Islands take their name.
dampac_manilo: According to Dampier, the name of the city otherwise called Manila at Luconia.
dampac_manilbo: According to Dampier, the name of the city otherwise called Manila at Luconia.
dampac_goodlud: According to Dampier, the name of the London captain who called at the Philippine Islands.
dampac_ternate: According to Dampier, the name of an island of the Spice Islands.
dampac_tidore: According to Dampier, the name of an island of the Spice Islands.
dampac_rofy: According to Dampier, the name of the ship commander who described the use of sago in the Spice Islands.
dampac_havana: According to Dampier, the name of a town named for its markets for plantains.
dampac_cartagena: According to Dampier, the name of a town named for its markets for plantains.
dampac_hilanoon: According to Dampier, the name of the people of the mountainous interior of Mindanao.
dampac_saggen: According to Dampier, the name of the local term for common plantain fibre cloth and its plant.
dampac_pagally: According to Dampier, the name of the local title for the other-sex friend who exchanges gifts in this account.

dampac_saker: According to Dampier, the name of the historical class of iron cannon seen in the reception chamber.
dampac_minion: According to Dampier, the name of the historical class of small cannon displayed with the sakers.
dampac_ramdam: According to Dampier, the name of the fasting month called Ramdam in this narrative.
dampac_gong: According to Dampier, the name of the single-headed mosque drum used to mark the hours on Mindanao.
dampac_thacker: According to Dampier, the name of one of Dampier’s companions visited at Mindanao.

dampac_leon: According to Dampier, the name of a town where Smith was taken prisoner in Dampier’s account.
dampac_henry: According to Dampier, the name of the given name of Henry More in this voyage.
dampac_tace: According to Dampier, the name of the Latin word quoted in Goodlud’s joke about keeping silent.
dampac_samo: According to Dampier, the name of the local word for sameness in the friendship demonstration reported by Dampier.
dampac_bugeto: According to Dampier, the name of the local expression for the separation demonstrated with the fingers.
dampac_wapping: According to Dampier, the name of a district where Thacker learned to dance.
dampac_bowry: According to Dampier, the name of the captain who wrote the letter about the supposed English factory.
dampac_reedjamaica: According to Dampier, the name of John Reed of Jamaica, the namesake criticized in the journal.
dampac_cookworthy: According to Dampier, the name of the man sent for medical attendance.
dampac_bristol: According to Dampier, the name of the city of the first John Reed.

dampac_jackal: The barking wild canid Dampier believed he heard in Mexico.
dampac_snook: The long-bodied coastal fish called snook by the sailors.
dampac_squall: A sudden fierce maritime squall in Dampier’s use of tornado.
dampac_jewfish: Dampier’s name for the large edible coastal fish.
dampac_volcano: A mountain whose summit emits volcanic fire or smoke.
dampac_penguinfruit: The fleshy fruit of the spiny tropical plant called penguin in the voyage.
dampac_landbreeze: Wind blowing offshore from the land.
dampac_seabreeze: Wind blowing onshore from the sea.
dampac_tradewind: Wind with a prevailing direction over a particular sea or coast.
dampac_savanna: Open tropical grassland as distinguished from the adjoining woodlands.
dampac_maize: The American grain distinguished by Dampier from other kinds of corn.
dampac_aboard: On or onto a vessel, as opposed to ashore.
dampac_capsize: To overturn a boat in the water.
dampac_abreast: Level with a landmark along a ship’s coastal track.
dampac_farm: A managed holding where crops or livestock are raised.
dampac_pork: Pig flesh eaten as food, whether fresh or preserved.
dampac_lagoon: A saltwater lake connected with the sea through a restricted mouth.
dampac_pilotbook: Written sailing directions and descriptions of coasts for pilots.
dampac_breastwork: A protective low fieldwork or embankment.
dampac_mixedman: The man described with the source’s historical racial designation at this particular landing.
dampac_equator: The imaginary circle used as the origin of terrestrial latitude.
dampac_calico: Cotton cloth carried in the Manila trade.
dampac_muslin: Fine lightweight cotton cloth traded through Manila.
dampac_tonnage: Historical ship carrying-capacity measure, distinct from a vessel for storing liquids.
dampac_landward: Toward or within the country away from the seashore.
dampac_notable: Easy to recognize from the sea by a distinctive visible form.
dampac_encourage: An opportunity or promising sign that leads a party to press on.
dampac_cruise: Sail about on a coast for a time awaiting an encounter, rather than making a direct passage.
dampac_makeable: To furnish the means or capacity to undertake what follows.
dampac_traffic: Contact and exchange across a passage of water.
dampac_fishery: The occupation or act of catching marine animals, including pearl oysters.
dampac_gunplatform: Raised emplacement on which the harbour artillery stands.
dampac_paddle: Move a canoe with a hand-held paddle, distinguished from rowing with oars in tholepins.
dampac_palmetto: The palm whose thatching is compared with the larger palm fronds.
dampac_cabbagepalm: Palm with a leafy crown likened to a cabbage.
dampac_mixedwoman: The woman identified by the source's colonial designation Mulatto at Petaplan.
dampac_hundredweight: English unit of commercial weight called a hundred weight in the fish description.
dampac_guava: Tropical fruit growing wild in this coastal valley.
dampac_limefruit: The small sour green citrus fruit, distinct from birdlime and mineral lime.
dampac_rockfish: Dampier's shore fish named for its rocky habitat, previously described at Juan Fernández.
dampac_catfish: Fish with whisker-like barbels caught at several places on the coast.
dampac_sounding: A depth measured by a sailor, or one of a series of depths taken towards the shore.
dampac_iguana: The large American lizard Dampier spells guano or guana.
dampac_mangrove: Trees of tidal flats and river mouths growing in salt water.
dampac_ninepin: One upright wooden pin in the knocking-down game of ninepins, used for the fruit's outline.
dampac_anus: The body's anal opening, called the fundament, distinguished from the whole buttocks.
dampac_parade: Central open ground of a Spanish town overlooked by houses and church.
dampac_balcony: A raised, projecting place fronting a house and overlooking the central square.
dampac_supercargo: Principal merchant responsible for the cargo and business aboard ship.
dampac_holster: Pistol case worn or carried at either side of a saddle.
dampac_carbine: Short gun borne by a mounted soldier, as seen on the riderless horse.
dampac_houseleek: Succulent plant named sempervive in the comparison of island roots.
dampac_burdock: The English weed whose boiled roots Dampier compares in taste with the island plant.
dampac_raccoon: American mammal compared by Dampier to a large rat.
dampac_striker: A fisherman skilled in striking swimming fish or turtles, distinct from a hook-and-line fisher.
dampac_coconut: Fruit of the coconut palm with fibrous husk and a hard shell enclosing nut water.
dampac_toddy: Palm sap collected for drinking and for subsequent fermentation.
dampac_arrack: The strong alcoholic spirit obtained by distilling palm wine.
dampac_coir: Cordage spun from the fibre of the coconut husk.
dampac_breadfruit: The starchy fruit islanders roast and eat as bread.
dampac_proa: The distinctive outrigger sailing canoe of the Marianas.
dampac_flyingfish: Fish that glide above the surface on their extended fins.
dampac_booby: The pelagic seabird named by Dampier, taken here as a sign of offshore rocks.
dampac_ration: An allotted share of food per crew member in a given period.
dampac_column: Vertical division of a tabulated set of observations.
dampac_logline: The log run out astern to estimate a vessel's speed and distance.
dampac_rhumb: A course along a constant point of the compass.
dampac_hydrographer: Maker of nautical charts and reckoner of the extent of seas.
dampac_rice: The grain sown or eaten on Guam and neighbouring islands.
dampac_watermelon: The large watery melon, distinguished by Dampier from muskmelon.
dampac_muskmelon: The fragrant melon contrasted with watermelon in the Guam fruit list.
dampac_magvar: Angular difference between the direction of the magnetic needle and geographic north.
dampac_seamate: Officer assisting the ship's master in navigation and command.
dampac_punch: Mixed drink made with spirit and citrus juice, distinguished here by the spirit used.
dampac_brandy: Strong spirit distilled from wine, used in the author's account to fortify the punch.
dampac_rasp: A toothed iron scraper for removing the edible kernel from the coconut shell.
dampac_oakum: Fibrous caulking for sealing the seams of ships.
dampac_lemontreefruit: The larger yellow citrus fruit contrasted with the smaller thin-rinded lime.
dampac_tapbranch: To notch or cut a fruiting branch so that its sap can be collected.
dampac_chili: The hot pod pepper called Guinea-pepper or cod-pepper in the account, distinct from ground black pepper.
dampac_mizzen: Aftermost mast with its obliquely slung yard, used here as a comparison.
dampac_sailreef: A portion of sail taken up to shorten its exposed area in wind, distinct from an underwater reef.
dampac_paddleblade: Broad hand-held steering blade, distinguished from a fixed rudder and from the action of paddling.
dampac_mango: Fleshy fruit of a tropical tree, here preserved in pickle.
dampac_monsoon: Seasonal reversal or prevailing seasonal wind that governs sailing between islands.
dampac_astrolabe: Instrument for taking angular heights of sun and stars.
dampac_rusk: Fine wheat bread baked to keep, compared with a softer ship biscuit.
dampac_reellog: Reel paying out the knotted line used to estimate a boat's speed.
dampac_brisket: The breast cut of beef used as the comparison for the firm texture of the pork.
dampac_laceband: An ornamental band woven with threads of silver or gold.
dampac_libby: The Libby palm whose pith is processed into an edible starch.
dampac_sago: The edible starch washed from the pith of the Libby palm.
dampac_banana: The sweet banana, distinguished by the narrator from the cooking plantain.
dampac_betelnut: The areca palm seed chewed with betel leaf and lime.
dampac_areca: The green-barked shrub called Arek in this source; Dampier uses its leaves for wrapping the nut.
dampac_durian: Strong-scented tropical fruit with a hard spiny rind and creamy edible flesh.
dampac_jackfruit: Large composite tropical fruit growing from the trunk of the jaca tree.
dampac_centipede: Many-legged arthropod that Dampier also calls Forty Legs.
dampac_clovebark: Fragrant bark distinguished from the clove buds of the Spice Islands.
dampac_treemouth: Soft internal tissue of the palm, distinct from the fibrous outer wood.
dampac_muslim: A follower of Islam, rendered from the source's period word Mahometan.
dampac_smuggle: Trade goods secretly in violation of the authorities' restrictions.
dampac_eldertree: The pithy elder shrub cited as a comparison for the pith of the libby palm.
dampac_pumpkin: The large gourd grown in the upland fields of Mindanao.
dampac_sucker: Young vegetative shoot growing from an older plantain root.
dampac_marmalade: Soft fruit preserve, illustrating the melting texture of ripe plantain flesh.
dampac_realcoin: Spanish real, whose half is quoted as the cost of a dozen plantains.
dampac_mishlaw: Moskito drink of roasted ripe plantain squeezed into water.
dampac_buffjacket: English seamen's name for a lump of boiled mashed ripe plantains.
dampac_lambswool: Apple and ale drink used to explain the taste of mishlaw.
dampac_agency: A commercial establishment maintained by a trading company abroad, called a factory.
dampac_bonito: The pelagic fish named Boneta in Dampier's list.
dampac_cavally: The fish called Cavally by Dampier, a type of jack, distinct from the jewfish and snook.
dampac_bream: The broad-bodied fish called a breme in the list of local catches.
dampac_mullet: The fish known as mullet, named among the Mindanao catches.
dampac_tenpounder: The fish called the ten-pounder, a common name rather than the measured weight of a specimen.
dampac_buffalo: Asian buffalo found among the animals of Mindanao.
dampac_parakeet: Small parrot in the list of wild birds of Mindanao.
dampac_barbhook: Backward-pointing projection on a hook, compared with the double tip of a lizard’s tongue.
dampac_giddiness: Feeling of the head spinning, attributed in the account to chewing old areca nut.
dampac_adze: A woodworking blade set across its handle for dressing a plank.
dampac_smallpox: The named smallpox illness distinguished from the skin condition previously described.
dampac_cylinder: A hollow cylindrical body as in the wooden bellows.
dampac_sultan: A sultan, the title of the ruler of Mindanao or another sultanate of the region in this account. The established native title is used independently of its Ottoman reference in Locke.
